title: Selected primary-source and novelty audit for the Yang–Mills workbench compendium
scope: Selected inspected sources, not an exhaustive literature or priority search. Research compendium draft; no new physics runs.
novelty_conclusion: Scientific novelty is not established. Explicit model-specific arithmetic, certificates, and scope counterexamples are candidate contributions requiring a dedicated priority comparison.

historical_ledger.method: Read and counted stored JSON rows; no study or physics calculation rerun.

bibliography.author: Wilson, Kenneth G.
bibliography.title: Confinement of quarks

references.inspected: Publisher metadata; original article, abstract and introduction, printed pp. 2445–2446 (PDF pp. 1–2).
references.established_method_or_hypotheses: Compact lattice links and strong-coupling reasoning are established. The introductory discussion treats the lattice as an ultraviolet cutoff.
references.workbench_relationship: Finite Haar integrations and graph identities should be presented as explicit computations within established lattice theory.
references.limitation: The strong-coupling cutoff model is not by itself a Lorentz-invariant continuum construction; the full expansion was not re-audited.
references.priority_status: not established by this selected review

bibliography.author: Yarotsky, D. A.
bibliography.title: Quasi-particles in weak perturbations of non-interacting quantum lattice systems

references.inspected: Setup and Theorem 1, PDF pp. 2–3.
references.established_method_or_hypotheses: Possibly infinite-dimensional sites have nonnegative self-adjoint onsite operators, a unique zero-energy vacuum, and a gap at least one. Bounded perturbations have a fixed finite support shape and sufficiently small uniform norm.
references.workbench_relationship: This supplies qualitative product-phase stability after an explicit model dictionary, including interaction blocking.
references.limitation: Smallness constants depend on the interaction geometry and are not numerically evaluated here. This citation cannot certify a particular workbench coupling.
references.priority_status: not established by this selected review

bibliography.author: Henheik, Joscha and Teufel, Stefan and Wessel, Tom
bibliography.title: Local stability of ground states in locally gapped and weakly interacting quantum spin systems

references.inspected: §2, Definitions 1–2 and Theorem 3; introduction on the relation to Yarotsky.
references.established_method_or_hypotheses: Unique gapped onsite ground states and sufficiently weak bounded finite-range interactions give exponentially small distant ground-state effects of a local perturbation with relative bound below one. Infinite onsite dimension is allowed.
references.workbench_relationship: Supports a carefully matched local-stability comparison, not an unqualified import of a numerical threshold.
references.limitation: The local perturbation can close the perturbed global gap. Theorem 3 is a locality statement about ground states, not a gap-preservation theorem for arbitrary local perturbations.
references.priority_status: not established by this selected review

bibliography.author: Bravyi, Sergey and DiVincenzo, David and Loss, Daniel
bibliography.title: Polynomial-time algorithm for simulation of weakly interacting quantum spin systems

references.inspected: §1, PDF pp. 3–5, Eqs. (1)–(6), Theorems 1–3.
references.established_method_or_hypotheses: Qubits on a bounded-degree graph have onsite gaps at least Δ and two-qubit interactions bounded by J. The stated explicit perturbative scale is ε₀=2⁻¹⁸Δ/(dJ).
references.workbench_relationship: Shows that explicit weak-interaction algorithms and thresholds are established in their stated setting.
references.limitation: The qubit/two-site theorem does not automatically cover infinite-dimensional SU(2) factors or arbitrary block interactions. This is not the later Schrieffer–Wolff paper.

bibliography.author: Del Vecchio, Simone and Fr{"o}hlich, J{"u}rg and Pizzo, Alessandro
bibliography.title: Block-diagonalization of infinite-volume lattice Hamiltonians with unbounded interactions

references.inspected: §§1.1–1.2, PDF pp. 3–5, Eqs. (1.3), (1.6)–(1.11); statement of Theorem 2.10, PDF p. 12.
references.established_method_or_hypotheses: Separable onsite spaces and unique gapped vacua are allowed. Finite-range symmetric interactions obey uniform local relative-form bounds, with the stated domain conditions or quadratic-form variant. A volume-independent sufficiently small coupling gives a gap.
references.workbench_relationship: This is a relevant existing route for rotor-type spaces. The workbench must match domains, geometry, weighted norms, and quantitative constants.
references.limitation: No blanket claim that block-diagonalization literature excludes unbounded onsite systems is justified. Full inductive estimates and a numerical translated threshold were not audited.

bibliography.author: Nachtergaele, Bruno and Sims, Robert
bibliography.title: On the dynamics of lattice systems with unbounded on-site terms in the Hamiltonian

references.inspected: §2, PDF pp. 2–6, including Proposition 2.1; §3, Theorem 3.1; finite-volume comparison around Eqs. (83)–(88).
references.established_method_or_hypotheses: Self-adjoint onsite terms on separable spaces coexist with bounded intersite interactions having finite F-norm. F is uniformly summable and has a finite convolution constant. Interaction-picture calculus controls local dynamics.
references.workbench_relationship: Provides a framework for the workbench’s spatial limits and locality bounds with unbounded onsite kinetic energy.
references.limitation: Spatial norm convergence on compact time intervals does not establish norm continuity in time on the full local bounded-operator algebra. Commutator limits need domain/topology control.

bibliography.author: Tong, Yu and Albert, Victor V. and McClean, Jarrod R. and Preskill, John and Su, Yuan
bibliography.title: Provably accurate simulation of gauge theories and bosonic systems

references.inspected: Appendix B, Eq. (24), and Appendix D, Theorem 6, Eqs. (62)–(67); the project’s earlier §2 reading is recorded separately.

bibliography.author: Teschl, Gerald
bibliography.title: Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics: With Applications to {Schr"odinger} Operators

references.inspected: §4.4, Corollary 4.13 and Theorem 4.14, printed p. 141; §4.5, Theorem 4.16, p. 142; §6.1, Theorem 6.4 and Lemma 6.5, p. 159.
references.established_method_or_hypotheses: Min–max and Temple bounds require the stated spectral separation and full-operator residual for a normalized domain vector. Kato–Rellich requires relative bound below one; the resolvent identity requires common resolvent points.

references.limitation: A compressed residual alone is insufficient; the correct Hilbert-space Gram and omitted channels matter. This is an author-hosted mathematical reference, not a claim of priority for the classical theorems.
